title: The approved range, the negotiation outcome vocabulary, the TCG-share column, the rule that authorises an out-of-range outcome and the guarantee payment event have no source in S3, and the state the story moves is the claim's and not the case's
source: Legacy RWB-E4-018 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, heading RWB-E4-018, sections Story, Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4, Data, Endpoints, Screen and states, Validation and messages, Guardrails); FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3 A2.6.1 to A2.6.4 and A2.4.3.1, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.1, T6.1 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-GUA-20 to R-GUA-29; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-05, DP-13, DP-19 and R7.3
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths X4, X5 and X8; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC3 and Target reading; 8 Business rules BR1, BR2, BR3 and BR8; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.3; 12.4; 12.7; 13 Solution plan Database and Configuration; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the application slice. (1) The approved range has no definition: the legacy criterion says 'within the range', R-GUA-28 says 'inside the approved range', the FSD A2.6.3.1 lists no range rule and no field, and the TSD S3 carries no range table, list or parameter, so the bounds, the unit and the owner of the range are stated by no source. (2) No rule identifier authorises a negotiation outcome outside the range: the FSD A2.6.3.1 names VR-S3-006-1, R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24, R-GUA-29 and BR-S3-006 only, so no approval path can be named and the outcome is refused. (3) The negotiation outcome has no vocabulary: no list of outcome values exists in the FSD, the TSD or LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, which holds PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED only. (4) The TCG share has no column and no field identifier: guarantee_claim stops at DF-TRT-022 and the LDM gives no share field, while AC2 and AC3 require the share to be recorded for all future recoveries. (5) No source names the event that carries a guarantee payment, and neither the ownership rows (0 events) nor Architecture v5 slide 13 settles whether the service subscribes to P8's events or receives the payment as a signal the parent forwards. (6) The guarantee_claim row carries status (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) but no field for the 17 GUARANTEE states of TSD S3 T4 other than the standard state column of T3.0, which is a working read. (7) The legacy Data table names recovery_case, case_party, assignment, timer and v_ace_customer, and none of them is this service's in the target.
evidence: FSD S3 v3 A2.6.3.1 (rules and messages only, no range, no outcome list) and A2.6.3.2 (the field catalog of guarantee_claim, no outcome and no share); TSD S3 v2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022, no share) and T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS, LOV-CLAIM-TYPE only); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-28 ('inside the approved range') and R-GUA-23/24 ('TCG holds a share of every later recovery'); legacy RWB-E4-018 AC1 to AC3 and Data; _work/msr/context/S3.md ownership rows (1 table, 2 REST operations, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow)
area: S3 application slice and values in force
owner_role: Business owner of module S3 with the rwb-guarantee tech lead and the solution architect
proposed: The range bounds, the notice expiry and the outcome list are added to the S3 reference-data register with their version and owner; the outcome list is published as LOV-NEG-OUTCOME; the TCG share is a numeric(18,2) column of guarantee_claim added by this story's Flyway version with its percentage basis recorded; the guarantee payment reaches the stage as a signal the parent forwards until the payment story publishes an event, and the subscription is then added to the event catalogue.

title: The story master, the functional specification and the technical specification disagree on who owns the state, on its vocabulary and on whom the outcome is recorded against
source: Legacy RWB-E4-018 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC3; FSD S3 v3 A2.6.1 ('record the outcome against the party') and A2.6.4.1 (AC-S3-006-01); TSD S3 v2 T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) and T4 (the GUARANTEE set, 32 rules over 17 states); Template and Rules v1 R3 (source precedence); _work/msr/context/S3.md
section: 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC2 and AC3 and Target reading; 8 Business rules BR2 and BR3; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.7; 15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the three disagreements of this legacy key. (1) Owner of the transition: AC2 and AC3 move 'the case' to SUBROGATION_POSITION, while TSD S3 T4 moves the GUARANTEE claim (CLAIM_PAID and CLAIM_PART_PAID to SUBROGATION_POSITION) and the case status belongs to rwb-case in the target, so the legacy line cannot be true as written once the case leaves this service. (2) Vocabulary: AC1 to AC3 name the GUARANTEE states of TSD S3 T4, the stored status column carries LOV-CLAIM-STATUS (PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED), and SCR-17 publishes a third list of labels (Not due, due, submitted, paid, refused); no source states the mapping between the three. (3) The party: the story master says the outcome is recorded 'against the customer', the functional specification says 'against the party', and neither names the record that holds it; the case party record is rwb-case's and the claim row has no party field.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-018 AC1 ('record the outcome against the customer'), AC2 and AC3 ('the case moves to SUBROGATION_POSITION') and Screen and states (SCR-17: Not due; due; submitted; paid; refused); FSD S3 v3 A2.6.1 ('against the party'); TSD S3 v2 T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS) and T4 (R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24 and the 17-state GUARANTEE set); _work/msr/context/S3.md (the case is P3, the workflow is GuaranteeClaimWorkflow, one table guarantee_claim)
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case and rwb-guarantee tech leads and the screen owners
proposed: SUBROGATION_POSITION and RESIDUAL_TO_ROUTE are read as the guarantee claim state of TSD S3 T4 carried on the standard state column, and the stage reports the outcome so that rwb-case moves and keeps the case; the three vocabularies are kept apart in the contract (state, status, screen label) with a documented mapping owned by the screen owners; the outcome is recorded against the claim and the party reference of the case, and the case-level record of the party stays with rwb-case.

title: The contract surface has no read operation, no negotiation element, no element name for the share and no entry format for the messages
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md ownership rows (2 REST operations provided: PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} and POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims; 1 table; 0 events; 0 jobs; 1 workflow); TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 (API-S3-001 and API-S3-002) and T-A.2 (GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaim, GuaranteeClaimUpdate); FSD S3 v3 A2.6.3.2 and Screens (SCR-17); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-13 and DP-19, R7.2 s12
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths X1 and X9; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 8 Business rules BR2, BR3 and BR5; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.7; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states; 16 Test cases TC-S3-E4018-CON-01
description: One combined row for the contract slice. (1) The service publishes two operations and neither is a read, so SCR-17 cannot read the claim through a published operation of rwb-guarantee and the read has to be the composite route's or a new operation that no ownership row gives. (2) The negotiation has no element: TSD S3 T-A.2 publishes GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaimUpdate and GuaranteeClaim only, and the body that carries the outcome, the outcome date and the range has no name and no property list in any source. (3) The TCG share has no element name and no type, although AC2 and AC3 require it to be recorded. (4) The entry format of a message in a published catalogue, and whether an error answer carries the merge fields or only the identifier, is stated by no source. (5) The TSD gives 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 as the error set but no message identifier per code, so the mapping of MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 to codes is a working read.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S3.md (REST operations provided: 2, neither a read); TSD S3 v2 T-A.1 (two endpoints), T-A.2 (three element names, errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503); FSD S3 v3 A2.6.3.2 (guarantee_claim fields, no outcome and no share) and Screens (SCR-17 reads the claim); legacy RWB-E4-018 Validation and messages (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003)
owner_role: Solution architect, S3, with the rwb-guarantee tech lead, the gateway-bff owner and the API owner
proposed: The claim surface stays at the two operations the ownership rows give and SCR-17 is composed by the gateway-bff route; the negotiation is carried on PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} as GuaranteeClaimUpdate; the share is published as subrogationShare with a numeric(18,2) basis; the message identifiers are mapped to 403, 422 and 503 and the catalogue entry format is fixed once with the platform library stories (DL10).
